The local-keycloak env commands require a locally-provisioned Keycloak + all secrets in config/runtime/local-keycloak.vars which is git-ignored and not provided. So the `env:up:local-keycloak` path is fundamentally not runnable in this clean workspace without external Keycloak infrastructure and secrets.

- Node 24.15.0 + pnpm 11.3.0 installed
- pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
- pnpm check:toolchain-consistency passed
- pnpm nx run sva-studio-react:verify:runtime-artifact passed (build + start + health checks against ephemeral Postgres/Redis/mock Keycloak)

That's strong objective evidence.

The compose files reference postgres/redis. There's no Keycloak service in compose. The local-keycloak profile expects an external Keycloak (svs-intern-studio-staging). Without base.vars/local-keycloak.vars (not in repo) and without a Keycloak server, it cannot run. Let me double-check if there's maybe a way - maybe base.vars can be constructed. But the docs explicitly say it's a canonical source under config/runtime and git-ignored, meaning the operator provides it. This is not something the agent can reconstruct faithfully (secrets, Keycloak URL).

But local-keycloak requires SVA_AUTH_ISSUER, SVA_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET etc. — there's no local Keycloak. It would fail at smoke/login. Building a fully working local-keycloak env from scratch is not feasible without secrets/external service. This is arguably an EXTERNAL_RESOURCE/DOCUMENTATION limitation.

Still, the primary install (dependency install + build + runtime verification) is objectively successful. Let me also try the dev server briefly to show the app starts? The verify already starts the production artifact and gets 200 on /, /health/live, /health/ready. That's sufficient.

Given limited time and that verify:runtime-artifact is the guide's mandated build proof, I think we're good.
